chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about one who performed *dhahir* in the month of Sha'ban and could not find what to free [a slave], so he said: He waits until he fasts the month of Ramadan, then he fasts two consecutive months. If he performed *dhahir* while he was a traveler, he waits until he arrives [home]. And if he fasted and then acquired wealth, he must complete what he began.

key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Dhahir if one cannot free a slave?
ai.summary: This narration from *al-Istibsar* details the graduated expiation for *Zihar*, prioritizing fasting when slave emancipation is unaffordable, with specific provisions for travelers and those who acquire wealth mid-fast. It highlights the Shia juristic view on the continuity of acts of worship once initiated, even if the primary obligation (freeing a slave) becomes feasible. The ruling underscores the flexibility of divine law in accommodating hardship while maintaining the integrity of the expiatory sequence.
